profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, labeled Datacenter TIM-Google, sits in the Moncalieri area just south of Turin, Italy, coordinates that place it at or very near Via Cruto 2, an address that data center directories list as Noovle DC Moncalieri, one of several facilities Noovle, the cloud subsidiary of Italian telecom TIM, operates around Turin. This registry could not independently confirm with full certainty this exact OSM point maps to that specific building rather than a neighboring Noovle or TIM site, and records that caveat honestly rather than asserting a precise match. The broader TIM-Google relationship began in March 2020, when TIM became a Google Cloud Premier Partner and migrated roughly 6,600 internal workloads, about 26 percent of its private cloud, onto Google Cloud infrastructure using Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine, and Anthos. TIM launched Noovle SpA as a dedicated cloud and edge subsidiary on January 25, 2021, which at launch managed 17 existing data centers nationwide and announced plans for 6 new Tier IV certified facilities targeting more than 50,000 square meters and 100 megawatts of usable IT power by 2022. Google Cloud opened its second Italian region in Turin on March 23, 2023, spanning 3 availability zones, built on Noovle operated data center capacity, with University of Turin research projecting a 3.3 billion euro economic impact for the Piedmont and Lombardy regions by 2025 and Politecnico di Milano estimating a 1.9 billion euro new partner ecosystem market for 2023 through 2025. Separate Noovle branded sites elsewhere in the Turin area, including Noovle DC Rivoli and a Cebrosa or Settimo Torinese site, are tracked as their own distinct rows in this registry rather than folded into this one, reflecting Noovles practice of operating multiple named buildings across the metropolitan area rather than a single consolidated TIM-Google campus.
